The contract confirms there are four sampled failures and only one editable policy file. I’m now anchoring the visual review to the parent guidance, observations, metrics, and inherited optimizer notes; no shelf or neighboring workspace evidence will be used.

The visuals separate the mechanisms cleanly: the seed self-propels leftward but is swept downward and exits, while the two damped target-feedback variants turn away and drift right with little useful propulsion. The strongest-progress controller does move left while holding roughly the correct vertical station, but its bend escalates into a tight loop and a force/moment blow-up. I’m cross-checking those behaviors against the exact sampled policies and inherited hypotheses before choosing a bounded revision.

The inherited logs confirm that derivative/rate steering has not produced a clean positive result. The reusable signal is instead a propulsion/stability tradeoff: full phase-radius regulation stayed low-load but became almost flow-following, while the position-only oscillator generated the only active upstream motion and then saturated. I’ll record the candidate hypothesis now, as required by the visual-inspection skill, before changing the policy.

The single candidate now preserves the progress-producing position-only oscillator, reduces curvature, and adds a policy-owned smooth acceleration shoulder that is linear across the nominal gait. The durable guidance now records the key negative lesson: low load is not useful when relative motion collapses to local-flow tracking, with a clear causal boundary. I’m invoking the required three-part non-CFD check runner now.

The first required check exposed a rendered-workspace defect: `README.md` contains the same copied-parent marker twice, so the checker cannot select one parent. I’m removing only that duplicate metadata entry, leaving the assigned parent unchanged, then rerunning the check.

The guidance check passes. The Julia contract command could not start because this workspace image has no `julia` executable on `PATH` (the preceding SSH-profile warnings are environmental). I’m checking for a nonstandard Julia installation and will still run the independent boundary/schema guards; no CFD is being invoked.

The final non-CFD checks now pass for guidance materiality, solver edit boundaries, and the deterministic parameter-schema guard. The nominal anterior acceleration is `1233.70 deg/time²`, below the limiter’s `1275 deg/time²` linear knee. The only unavailable check is Julia execution itself because no Julia runtime exists in the image; I’m doing a final file/diff audit so that limitation is reported precisely.

The final audit confirms one notes file, one assigned-parent marker, one material guidance lesson, and only the permitted solver file changed. I’m also invoking the named `check-runner` independently, as the workspace contract requests, for a second read-only validation.
